header.title: Suppl. Mag. 42: Love spell (lesbian) with assistance of a demon, partly in iambic trimeter and choliambics: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Supplementum Magicum
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:92863:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.1.1: 1.6 is syntactically difficult and the sense of its opening clause is uncertain. ‘Become a bath-woman’ (1.14) is addressed to the daimon. Gorgonia, Nilogenia, Sophia and Isara are personal names.
notes.1.24: 1.25–30 are almost wholly voces magicae, transliterated and not translated; Ereschigal is the Mesopotamian underworld goddess Ereshkigal. ‘Tail-tip-devourer’ (1.30) renders the Greek epithet ἀκρουροβόρε. In 1.24 ‘all-wise and a boy’ is uncertain in sense; the ‘messenger’ is perhaps Hermes.
notes.1.54: ‘melike⟨r⟩tōr’ (1.57), between the epithets ‘honey-holder’ and ‘honey-begetter’, is left untranslated: its sense is unclear. A lacuna of unknown length in 1.55.

nodes.text: Seat of hateful darkness, jagged-toothed
hound, serpent-coiled, turner of three heads,
roamer of the depths, come, driver of spirits, with the Erinyes
made savage with bitter whips; sacred serpents, maenads,
dread maidens, come to my wrathful [incan]tations;
before I must win ⟨you⟩ over by force, swiftly make this fire-breathing
*daimōn* [spirit] [act]; listen, and make everything be done quickly, setting yourself against
me in nothing; for you are the rulers of the earth. alalachos allēch Harmachi-
meneus magimeneus athinembēs astazabathos artazabathos ōkoum
phlom lonchachinachana thou Azaēl and Lykaēl and Beliam and Belenēa
and sochsocham somochan sozocham ouzacham bauzacham oueddouch; through this
corpse-*daimōn* burn the heart, the liver, the spirit of Gorgonia, whom Nilogenia bore,
with love and affection for Sophia, whom Isara bore; compel Gorgonia, whom Nilogenia
bore, to be cast to Sophia, whom Isara bore, into the bath-house; and become a bath-woman; burn, set on fire,
inflame the soul, the heart, the liver, the spirit with love for Sophia, whom Isara bore; lead
Gorgonia, whom Nilogenia bore, lead her, torment her body night and day, force
her to rush out from every place and every house, loving Sophia, whom Isara bore, handed over
like a slave, giving herself and all her possessions to her, because this is willed and commanded by the great
